1.note: Yahweh is using a word that expresses a strong feeling of urgent invitation. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Hey]

The implied word **you** is plural in these imperatives even though the addressee, “to whom is no silver” is singular, because Yahweh is addressing the Israelites as a group, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is speaking of the people’s need for what he offers as if it were physical thirst, inviting **everyone thirsty** to **go to the waters**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everyone who longs for what I offer, come to me and receive it]
In a context such as this, your language might say “come” instead of **go**. Alternate translation: [come to the waters … come, buy, and eat … And come]

2.q: לָ֤⁠מָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ־כֶ֨סֶף֙ בְּֽ⁠לוֹא־לֶ֔חֶם וִ⁠יגִיעֲ⁠כֶ֖ם בְּ⁠ל֣וֹא לְ⁠שָׂבְעָ֑ה שִׁמְע֨וּ שָׁמ֤וֹעַ אֵלַ⁠י֙ וְ⁠אִכְלוּ־ט֔וֹב וְ⁠תִתְעַנַּ֥ג בַּ⁠דֶּ֖שֶׁן נַפְשְׁ⁠כֶֽם
2.note: The words **you** and **your** and the implied “you” in the imperatives **listen** and **eat** are plural because Yahweh is addressing the people of Israel. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

2.q: לָ֤⁠מָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ־כֶ֨סֶף֙ בְּֽ⁠לוֹא־לֶ֔חֶם וִ⁠יגִיעֲ⁠כֶ֖ם בְּ⁠ל֣וֹא לְ⁠שָׂבְעָ֑ה
2.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people for spending their resources on what does not truly nourish or satisfy them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not weigh out silver for what is not bread, nor your labor for what does not satisfy!]

Yahweh is speaking of spending effort and money on things that do not satisfy as if it were paying **silver** for something that is **not bread**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do you pay silver for what cannot sustain you]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **listen** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Listen very carefully to me]

Here, **your soul** represents the whole person, that is, you yourself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [yourself]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fatness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by rich food] or [by abundant food]

3.note: Yahweh is using **Incline your ear** as a common expression of the culture to mean “listen carefully.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Listen carefully]
In a context such as this, your language might say “come” instead of **go**. Alternate translation: [and come to me]

Yahweh is using the expression **cut with you a covenant** as a common expression of the culture to mean “make a covenant with you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [make a covenant with you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulnesses**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the faithful deeds I promised to David]

4.note: Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen]
The pronoun **him** refers to David. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I have given David]

The terms **a ruler** and **a commander** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [a supreme ruler]

5.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 55:4.

The possessive form **Yahweh your God** does not indicate that the people possess or control Yahweh. Rather, it indicates that Yahweh is the God whom the people worship. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, the God whom you worship]

6.note: The expression **he may be found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [while you can find him]

7.note: Yahweh is speaking of the wicked person’s conduct as if it were a **way** or road that he travels. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his sinful conduct]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and let the man of iniquity abandon his thoughts]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [and the person of iniquity]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [wicked deeds]

Yahweh is speaking of turning away from sin and coming back to God as if the person could physically **return to Yahweh**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let him come back to Yahweh in repentance]

The possessive form **our God** does not indicate that Isaiah and the people possess or control Yahweh. Rather, it indicates that Yahweh is the God whom they worship. Alternate translation: [the God whom we worship]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because he will abundantly forgive]

8.note: Isaiah is using **Yahweh declares** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

9.q: גָבְה֥וּ שָׁמַ֖יִם מֵ⁠אָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֣ן גָּבְה֤וּ דְרָכַ⁠י֙ מִ⁠דַּרְכֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וּ⁠מַחְשְׁבֹתַ֖⁠י מִ⁠מַּחְשְׁבֹתֵי⁠כֶֽם
9.note: The point of this comparison is that, just as **the heavens are higher than the earth**, so also **my ways are higher than your ways, and my thoughts, than your thoughts**. Yahweh means that his ways and thoughts are far above and beyond those of human beings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [my ways are far above your ways, and my thoughts far above your thoughts, as much as the heavens are above the earth]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and my thoughts are higher than your thoughts]

10.q: כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵרֵד֩ הַ⁠גֶּ֨שֶׁם וְ⁠הַ⁠שֶּׁ֜לֶג מִן הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְ⁠שָׁ֨מָּ⁠ה֙ לֹ֣א יָשׁ֔וּב כִּ֚י אִם הִרְוָ֣ה אֶת הָ⁠אָ֔רֶץ
10.note: Including verse 11, the point of this comparison is that, just as **the rain and snow come down from the heavens and do not return to there** until they have watered the earth and made it fruitful, so God’s word always accomplishes the purpose for which he sends it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [just as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not go back until they have watered the earth and made it produce, so also my word accomplishes my purpose before it returns to me]

The terms **the rain** and **snow** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [two forms of precipitation]

If it would appear in your language that Yahweh was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [but rather, they saturate the earth]

The terms **made it bring forth** and **made it sprout** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and made plants sprout abundantly from it]

11.q: יִֽהְיֶ֤ה דְבָרִ⁠י֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִ⁠פִּ֔⁠י לֹֽא־יָשׁ֥וּב אֵלַ֖⁠י רֵיקָ֑ם
11.note: Yahweh is speaking of **my word** as if it were a living thing that could go out, accomplish a task, and return to report. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when I declare something, I will certainly accomplish it and will not fail to bring it about]
Here, **my mouth** represents Yahweh’s act of speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [when I speak]

Yahweh is using **it will not return to me empty** as a common expression of the culture to mean that his word will not fail to accomplish its purpose. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it will not come back to me having accomplished nothing] or [it will not fail to accomplish what it was sent to do]

11.q: עָשָׂה֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפַ֔צְתִּי וְ⁠הִצְלִ֖יחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר & שְׁלַחְתִּֽי⁠ו
11.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [it will certainly accomplish everything I sent it to do]

12.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **joy** and **peace**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [joyfully, and you will be led peacefully]

The expression **you will be led** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will guide you]

The terms **The mountains** and **the hills** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [The great mountains]
Here, **your faces** represents your presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in your presence]

Yahweh is speaking of **all of the trees of the field** as if they were living things that could **clap the palm**, that is, clap their hands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and all of the trees of the field will be like people clapping their hands]

13.q: תַּ֤חַת הַֽ⁠נַּעֲצוּץ֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה בְר֔וֹשׁ תחת הַ⁠סִּרְפַּ֖ד יַעֲלֶ֣ה הֲדַ֑ס
13.note: Yahweh is speaking of the blessing and restoration he will bring as if worthless plants like **the thornbush** and **the nettle** would be replaced by valuable trees like **the cypress** and **the myrtle**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will replace everything worthless in your land with what is excellent]
Here, **a name** represents Yahweh’s renown or reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for renown]

The expression **it will not be cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will ever cut it off]
